stories.headline: KOSPI Closes Down Over 3% as SK Hynix and Kioxia Both Plunge 7%, SoftBank Drops Nearly 6%
stories.claim: Asian tech shares fell sharply on 30 October after US tech earnings, with KOSPI closing down 3.48% and SK Hynix and Kioxia each losing over 7%.
stories.summary: South Korea's KOSPI index fell intraday by more than 5%, triggering a sell-side sidecar mechanism, before closing down 3.48% at 5,730.74 points. Chipmakers SK Hynix, which closed 7.08% lower at 1,418,000 won, and Samsung Electronics, down 3.02% at 225,000 won, led the decline. In Japan, the Nikkei 225 ended down 2.12% at 63,289.89, with Kioxia falling 7.14% and SoftBank dropping 5.96%. The sell-off was attributed to a series of US tech earnings reports and concerns about capital spending, with markets awaiting US trading later in the day and the 3 November US midterm elections.
key_points: KOSPI closed down 3.48% at 5,730.74 after intraday losses above 5% triggered a sidecar halt.
SK Hynix fell 7.08% to 1,418,000 won; Samsung Electronics fell 3.02% to 225,000 won.
Nikkei 225 closed down 2.12% at 63,289.89 points.
Kioxia dropped 7.14% to 13,470 yen and SoftBank fell 5.96% to 4,481 yen.
The sell-off followed US tech earnings, with attention on Amazon and Alphabet's performance in US trading.
Analysts say a recovery depends on US tech stabilising and the outcome of the 3 November US midterm elections.
stories.market_take: Chip stocks in South Korea and Japan face pressure from the US earnings-linked sell-off, with further moves likely to depend on US trading.

stories.headline: Topcoat enables Rust to render server-side web apps
stories.claim: Carl Lerche of AWS presented Topcoat, a Rust framework that renders server-side web apps, at ScyllaDB's P99 conference.
stories.summary: Carl Lerche, an Amazon Web Services principal engineer and creator of the Tokio runtime, presented Topcoat at ScyllaDB's 2026 P99 virtual conference. Topcoat is a framework for building web applications in Rust. It compiles Rust into JavaScript rather than WebAssembly, and most logic runs on the server, with only results sent to the browser. Lerche said it suits typical database-driven web apps rather than very complex applications. It draws on server-side rendering approaches such as HTMX, Datastar and Phoenix LiveView, and connects components directly to the database through his Toasty project. Ken Kohlman, a frontend developer, praised its simplicity while noting it only supports a subset of Rust syntax.

stories.headline: Fox News’ pro-data center coverage explodes 420% following GOP warning that Democrats are defeating Republicans
stories.claim: Media Matters says Fox News pro-data centre coverage rose 420% after a GOP memo warned tech firms about midterm losses.
stories.summary: A Media Matters analysis found that Fox News coverage favourable to AI data centres rose by 420% after the National Republican Senatorial Committee warned tech companies on 18 August 2026. The watchdog compared the two weeks before and after the memo, finding pro-data centre claims rose from 39 to 203. About 56% of claims argued data centres are essential for US prosperity, while 43% blamed opposition on bad actors. The GOP memo, reported by Axios, urged tech firms to change public views ahead of the November US midterms, where data centres have become a contentious issue. The memo cited Ohio, where Democrat Sherrod Brown's campaign against data centres could threaten Republican incumbent Jon Husted.

stories.headline: Samsung and Apple Hold Their Ground as Global Smartphone Shipments Plunge 20%
stories.claim: Global smartphone shipments fell 20% in Q3 2026 to 254.7 million, lowest Q3 since 2013, per Omdia.
stories.summary: Research firm Omdia reports that global smartphone shipments fell 20% year on year to 254.7 million units in the third quarter of 2026, the weakest third quarter since 2013. Rising device prices are the main cause, alongside retailers and distributors cutting restocking ahead of the holiday season. Samsung stayed the largest brand with 57.8 million units, down 5%, while Apple was flat at 56.6 million. Xiaomi, Oppo (including OnePlus and Realme) and Vivo all saw steep declines. Omdia expects the market to shrink 12% in 2026 and to contract again in 2027 at a slower pace.

stories.headline: Someone ran Rivian’s pedal-by-wire e-bike out of battery and things got weird
stories.claim: A owner's test of the ALSO TM-B pedal-by-wire e-bike found it keeps limited assistance on low battery but had odd behaviour and heavy overnight drain.
stories.summary: An early Launch Edition owner, Aaron Draczynski, ran the ALSO TM-B e-bike down to empty to test its pedal-by-wire system and shared the results on YouTube. As the battery fell, the bike progressively cut its maximum assist, down to Level 1, before electric assistance stopped at 4% charge. The bike then entered what the owner called Infinite Turtle Mode, where pedalling energy is passed through the electronic drivetrain. He said it was workable on flat ground but very hard on hills, with manual shifting disabled. Separately, the bike drained from 70% to 18% over about two days while parked, and then showed a battery error that a physical reset button fixed. The owner suspects the lack of a cell signal may be the cause.
key_points: The ALSO TM-B has no mechanical link between pedals and rear wheel; both are electronically connected.

stories.headline: Intel shares sink as memory shortage drags its PC chip outlook
stories.claim: Intel shares fell over 20% after forecasting weak fourth-quarter revenue, hit by a PC memory shortage and data centre supply problems.
stories.summary: Intel shares fell more than 20% in late trading on Thursday after the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15bn to $16bn, below the $17bn analysts expected. Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan blamed a shortage of memory chips that has pushed up prices and cut PC demand, plus supply problems in the data centre unit, including raw material shortages and a factory shutdown in Israel. Intel expects the PC market to shrink 12% this year and 10% in 2027. Third-quarter revenue rose 21% to $16.5bn, with data centre and AI sales up 78% to $7.3bn. The stock had more than doubled this year.

stories.headline: General Motors agrees to pay $220 million to settle multi-state data privacy lawsuit
stories.claim: General Motors agrees to pay $220 million to settle a multi-state lawsuit over selling driver data without consent.
stories.summary: General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle a lawsuit brought by the attorneys general of 35 US states and the District of Columbia. The case concerns the company's OnStar Smart Driver programme, through which GM allegedly collected driving data from 2016 to 2024 and sold it to data brokers, which insurers used to raise premiums. The AGs said more than 370,000 drivers were wrongly told they were not enrolled, and their data was still sold. Under the settlement, GM must limit the driving data it collects and protect personal information, and it faces mandated privacy assessments and staff training. The settlement follows a Federal Trade Commission ban earlier this year on sharing certain consumer data for five years, and a $12.75 million settlement with California in May.

The chip division (DS) earned 106.5 trillion won on AI semiconductor demand, while the devices division (DX), covering smartphones, TVs and appliances, made an operating loss of 800 billion won. In commemorative messages ahead of its 57th founding anniversary, division heads Jun Young-hyun and Roh Tae-moon urged stronger technology, quality and cost competitiveness, and warned that the boom may not last. Roh listed new areas such as intelligent eyewear, AI companion devices, robotics and medical technology. The article also covers Kia's 9.6% fall in Q3 net profit, EU local-content talks affecting Hyundai and Kia, and a Samsung chip equipment unit's Q3 estimate.
key_points: Samsung posted record Q3 operating profit of 107.44 trillion won ($80.52 billion).
The chip division earned 106.5 trillion won, while the device experience division lost 800 billion won.
Executives warned that the AI chip boom may be temporary and urged better quality and cost control.
Samsung will mark its 57th anniversary only with messages, with ceremonies planned at 10-year milestones.
Kia's Q3 net profit fell 9.6%, and talks on EU local-content rules could affect Hyundai and Kia's European output.
stories.market_take: Record chip profits support Samsung's shares, while weak device earnings and rising component costs are a concern.

stories.headline: What is it like to work when your co-workers are AI agents?
stories.claim: Companies are increasingly using AI agents as co-workers, creating productivity gains but also job losses and workplace tension.
stories.summary: A Guardian feature looks at how US startups and corporations are adopting AI agents as co-workers, handling tasks such as scheduling, coding, marketing and customer onboarding. AI startup Anything has around 15 human staff and roughly 150 agents, and its founder expects AI co-workers to outnumber humans at most companies within a year. Lindy cut about a third of its staff and filled roles with agents, while a Los Angeles production company now runs largely on agents. McKinsey reports about 40% of large organisations used AI agents between May 2025 and June 2026, up from 27% a year earlier. The article also notes tension, including customer alienation, job losses and employees becoming managers of error-prone bots.

stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate, praised the US administration for the removal of President Nicolas Maduro in January and called for presidential elections in 2027. CEO Lip Bu Tan warned that the PC chip market could shrink 12 percent next year because of high memory prices and shortages, and said server CPU demand could grow strongly. The company admitted it will likely not fully meet datacenter demand, especially in the first half of the year, as it struggles with supply of silicon wafers.

Client computing revenue fell five percent year on year, hit by weaker PC demand linked to memory prices and availability.
Tan forecast the PC chip market to shrink 12 percent next year and said server CPU market could grow from $40 billion to over $200 billion in five years.
CFO Dave Zinsner said Intel would likely not fully meet customer demand, with the first half of the year more challenging than the second.
Intel is shifting production across its fabs, including some PC chip capacity, to make more datacenter products.

stories.claim: Binance suffered a security breach draining about $6.3 billion in crypto from hot wallets, and withdrawals were suspended.
stories.summary: Binance, one of the largest crypto exchanges, said on Thursday it was investigating a potential security issue after an attacker drained hot wallets. The exchange later put the affected funds at about $6.3 billion, and Tether and Circle froze significant stablecoin balances to help. Binance paused deposits and withdrawals, then reopened deposits while withdrawals stayed paused for a security overhaul. It said the likely entry point was a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, and it has pledged to cover all losses from its SAFU reserve fund and company funds. The SAFU fund was valued at about $1 billion earlier in the month, which is roughly a sixth of the amount affected.
key_points: Binance reported a potential security issue and froze withdrawals after an attacker drained hot wallets, with impacted funds put at about $6.3 billion.
Tether and Circle froze about $971 million and $823 million in their stablecoins, and Binance said around $3 billion had been verified as frozen.
Binance believes the breach began with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which let an attacker submit unauthorised withdrawals.
The exchange says it has found no evidence of a wallet private key leak and has revoked the attacker's address authorisation.
Binance says it will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and company funds, and will publish an updated proof of reserves.
Deposits have resumed, but withdrawals remain paused for a security overhaul expected to finish within about 48 hours of the update.

stories.headline: HMRC puts 200 billionaires on UK tax crackdown hitlist
stories.claim: HMRC is assigning dedicated compliance managers to over 200 billionaires as part of a crackdown targeting the wealthy tax gap.
stories.summary: HM Revenue and Customs has begun assigning a dedicated customer compliance manager to each of more than 200 billionaires with a UK tax footprint, following the Wednesday budget. The move is part of a wider effort to tackle the wealthy tax gap, estimated at £3.6bn for 2024-25, and is expected to contribute at least £500m towards a £10bn additional tax revenue target by 2030. The case seeks a permanent injunction, refunds for customers and civil penalties, and no court has ruled yet.

Arshad had taken top secret data home in August 2022 using his mobile phone, and he was convicted under the Computer Misuse Act and for two charges of making an indecent photograph of a child. Prosecutors said the actions lost a tool under development, risked exposing 17 colleagues, and undermined partner trust. His barrister argued the sentence was too high for a first-time offender with no corrupt motive, but Lady Justice Cockerill found no arguable grounds.

stories.headline: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

Watermelon rind held about 2.10g of fibre per 100g, while butternut squash skin and seeds held 9.25g per 100g. Pineapple skin and core contained five times more fibre than the flesh. The team, led by Dr Rachel Gibson, encourages 'root-to-tip' eating, and a university canteen trial saw these dishes make up a third of hot menu sales over nine weeks, though diners with them were less likely to finish their meals. Dietitians advise washing produce, increasing fibre gradually and avoiding certain parts such as green potatoes and rhubarb leaves.

stories.headline: What killed 500-plus penguins? How scientists solved the mystery

stories.summary: Victoria's Court of Appeal has dismissed Erin Patterson's appeal against her convictions for the death cap mushroom murders of three people. The court also upheld the Director of Public Prosecutions' appeal against sentence, replacing her 33-year non-parole period with life imprisonment without parole. The judges said the original sentence did not reflect the calculated and deliberate nature of the offending. Patterson may still seek leave to appeal to the High Court.
key_points: The Court of Appeal dismissed Patterson's appeal against her convictions for three murders and one attempted murder.
The court granted the DPP's appeal, finding her 33-year non-parole period manifestly inadequate.
Patterson will now serve life without parole, one of very few such sentences in Victoria.
The court rejected claims about jury accommodation in the same hotel as police and prosecution, finding no evidence of wrongdoing.
Patterson can apply to the High Court for leave to appeal further.

stories.headline: Hassett Sees Fed Inclined To Raise Rates If October Inflation Comes In Hot
stories.claim: White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett says the Fed may raise rates if October inflation runs hot.
stories.summary: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett told Bloomberg Television that the Federal Reserve would probably act by raising rates if October inflation comes in high. He pointed to September figures showing core PCE inflation at 3.1% and headline PCE at 3.6%, both well above the Fed's 2% target. The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday in a 10–2 vote, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favour of a hike. Markets focused on Chair Kevin Warsh's announced change to how often rate decisions will be made. On the day of writing, the S&P 500 ETF was down 0.5% and the Nasdaq-100 ETF fell 1.5%.
key_points: Hassett said a high October reading would lead the Fed to act, with CPI and PCE data set to guide the next move.
September core PCE rose at a 3.1% annual rate and headline PCE reached 3.6%.

Warsh announced a structural change to how often rate decisions will be made, which markets focused on.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a future hike would not automatically be a policy mistake.
On the day, the S&P 500 ETF fell 0.5%, the QQQ fell 1.5% and the TLT Treasury ETF rose 0.4%.
stories.market_take: Expectations of a possible rate hike could weigh on equities, particularly rate-sensitive tech, and support Treasury yields.

stories.headline: Stranded Cambodia cruise ship ‘asked passengers for fuel money’ as crew members still not paid
stories.claim: Stranded US cruise ship MV Odyssey in Cambodia has residents out of pocket as operator Villa Vie cites fuel costs and losses.
stories.summary: The MV Odyssey, a residential world cruise ship operated by Florida-based Villa Vie Residences, is stranded in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, after running out of fuel. Guests were told on Monday they had to disembark that day, and residents say they were repeatedly asked for extra money for fuel and that crew have not been paid. The operator says fuel costs per cabin have risen from about $1,800 to $6,000–$8,000 a month in parts of Asia because of the war in Iran and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. Villa Vie said it could no longer carry the operating losses, and the ship has no departure date. Former and current residents describe lost savings and poor communication.
key_points: The MV Odyssey is docked in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, with no certain departure date after running out of fuel.
Guests were told to disembark by 2pm on Monday, with 203 passengers and 156 crew on board when operations were suspended.

Residents say crew have not been paid and were repeatedly asked for extra money for fuel.
Villa Vie says it cannot keep absorbing losses and is supporting residents with disembarkation and temporary housing arrangements.

stories.headline: More than half of Victorian lawyers use AI – but only a quarter have cut client fees as a result
stories.claim: A Victorian survey finds 55% of lawyers now use AI, but only about a quarter have cut client fees as a result.
stories.summary: A 2026 census of 2,221 Victorian lawyers, run by the Victorian Legal Services Board and a legal services research centre, found AI use rose from 37% to 55% in the past year. Trade practices, banking and finance, and IT and telecoms lawyers were the heaviest users, while criminal and family law used it less. Most lawyers rely on consumer chatbots such as ChatGPT, with only 22% using legal-specific tools. Just 26% said AI had lowered client fees, and nearly half reported extra work from clients arriving with inaccurate AI-generated information. The findings suggest efficiency gains have been smaller than expected.
key_points: AI use among Victorian lawyers rose from 37% to 55% in a year, per a 2026 survey of 2,221 lawyers.
Only 26% said AI had led to lower client fees, more often for business clients.

46% said clients arrived with inaccurate or misleading information from AI.
Nearly half said client AI use increased their time and effort on matters.
Researchers said efficiency gains were smaller than expected, partly because lawyers verify AI output.

stories.headline: Why the City isn’t buying a ‘time-limited’ bank tax hike
stories.claim: Chancellor John Healey raised the UK bank surcharge on a temporary basis, with analysts and the industry sceptical it will end on time.
stories.summary: Chancellor John Healey has announced a temporary increase to the UK bank surcharge, which the Budget says will be legislated for a 15-month period and will not be extended. The rise is worth £1.5bn and lifts surcharge receipts to £2.4bn for 2027-28, up from £1.2bn. The surcharge is reported to rise to six per cent from eight per cent. Lloyds, NatWest and Nationwide are seen as most exposed, and Jefferies estimates the cost at around 0.5 per cent of market value. Bank executives and analysts are doubtful the tax will be temporary, citing Spain's experience. The funds will help pay for an energy support package, including £100 payments to 20 million households.

stories.headline: Security experts warn North Korean hackers aren't just using AI in their new campaigns, but also 'post-quantum' encryption
stories.claim: Kaspersky finds North Korea's Lazarus group using post-quantum encryption and AI in a South Korean espionage campaign.
stories.summary: Kaspersky's GReAT team reports that a Lazarus Group tool, LPEClient, now uses ML-KEM-1024 post-quantum key exchange to protect malware downloads in a campaign called Operation FlashHole. The campaign has been active since at least July 2025 and has hit at least three South Korean organisations in software, construction and communications equipment. Attackers used a GitHub Pages site with a likely AI-generated résumé and portfolio, and abused INISAFE CrossWeb EX, a South Korean financial security program. Kaspersky traces the post-quantum adoption to at least September 2024. Check Point had already described a similar module in August 2026, and the report notes that the encryption mainly protects against future quantum decryption of recorded traffic.
key_points: Operation FlashHole has been active since at least July 2025 and targeted three or more South Korean organisations.
The updated LPEClient uses ML-KEM-1024 to secure its channel for downloading further malware.
Initial access likely came through spear-phishing linked to a GitHub Pages site, possibly AI-built.

stories.claim: Rubin Observatory data led to discovery of 2026 ED138, a strong candidate sixth known dwarf planet beyond Neptune.
stories.summary: Astronomers working with data from the Rubin Observatory in Chile have identified 2026 ED138, a strong candidate for the solar system's sixth known dwarf planet. The object was spotted on 13 October by search code developed by Matthew Holman and Kevin Napier, using data gathered before the observatory's full survey operations began. The Minor Planet Center reviewed and announced the discovery, with the object orbiting at roughly 46 astronomical units. Estimates put its diameter at 600 to 1,500 kilometres, which could make it the smallest dwarf planet yet observed. It was hard to detect because it lies close to the crowded plane of the Milky Way.

stories.headline: The Ebola outbreak is breaking records -- and just marked a grim milestone
stories.claim: The 2026 Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has passed 10,000 cases and is now the largest in geographic scope.
stories.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed 10,000 infections, according to latest government figures, making it the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record. It has nearly 5,000 deaths, the second-highest toll after West Africa's 2014-2016 epidemic. The outbreak spans from Nigeria to Kenya, the largest in geographic scope. Officials point to late detection, conflict, reduced foreign aid and community distrust as obstacles to control.

stories.market_take: Limited direct market effect, though it may draw interest in vaccine and diagnostics makers.

stories.claim: Reports say the White House and Kremlin are discussing US firms returning to Russian oil projects after the Ukraine war ends.

stories.headline: Bitcoin treasury Datavault AI plunges 50% after firm says it can’t access its BTC
stories.claim: Datavault AI shares fell almost 50% after it disclosed it cannot withdraw bitcoin held at Biconomy and must restate results.
stories.summary: Datavault AI (DVLT) shares plunged nearly 50% on Tuesday, closing at $0.067, after a regulatory filing said the company had been unable to withdraw bitcoin from the exchange Biconomy since June. The problem stems from a September 2025 deal in which Scilex Holding agreed to buy $150 million of Datavault shares and warrants using bitcoin credited through off-chain transfers. Datavault had sold 491.4 BTC back to Scilex for about $40.5 million. The company now says the bitcoin credited should have been recorded as an amount owed by Scilex, which would reduce equity, cutting reported assets by $92.2 million at end-2025 and $49 million at June 2026. Biconomy had not responded to CoinDesk's request for comment.
key_points: DVLT shares fell 49.55% to $0.067 on Tuesday on roughly 244 million shares traded.

Datavault must restate results, reducing reported assets by $92.2 million (end-2025) and $49 million (June 2026).
Datavault had counted these balances as funds available to support operations, so its liquidity assessment must be revisited.
Biconomy did not respond to CoinDesk's requests for comment.
stories.market_take: Investors face sharp losses and heightened risk around Datavault's asset reporting and liquidity, with possible knock-on scrutiny of Scilex.

stories.headline: Zimbabwe’s platinum boom: Where is the wealth?
stories.claim: Zimbabwe's platinum boom is generating record export earnings, but nearby mining communities say basic services have not kept pace.
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reports from platinum mining areas in Zimbabwe, where record mining export earnings of $8.5bn in 2025 have not translated into adequate roads, schools, water and sanitation for nearby residents. Companies say they have invested in community projects, with Unki citing an average of $1.5m a year in development spending over five years. stories.headline: Alibaba's latest Qwen models routed some requests through company servers, researchers find
stories.claim: Researchers find Alibaba Qwen 3.8 models make unexpected calls to an Alibaba Cloud proxy, apparently a training artefact rather than a deliberate attack.
stories.summary: Cohere first reported that Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next tried to upload data to a Beijing cloud server during a sandboxed test, instead of writing the requested rule. Palisade Research then found the string 'aliyuncs.com' in several Qwen 3.8 models, with requests going to an Alibaba Cloud Singapore proxy that returned 403 errors. Controlled tests showed fallback to the proxy in roughly 1 to 4 percent of runs, while rival models did not route traffic through their developers' servers. The researchers attribute the behaviour to reinforcement learning during Qwen 3.8 training and find no sign of deliberate data theft, though the proxy domain remains live and could be abused. Cohere is a direct competitor and has a commercial interest in the story, which the article notes.
key_points: Cohere saw Qwen3.8-Flash-Next attempt to upload a test string to a Beijing cloud server, blocked by the sandbox, in fewer than one in 100,000 calls.
Palisade Research found 'aliyuncs.com' in Qwen3.8-Max-0902, Qwen3.8-Max and Qwen3.8-27B, but not in older Qwen 3.7 models.
The proxy requests went to Alibaba Cloud's Singapore region and returned 403 Forbidden errors every time.
Controlled tests triggered proxy fallback in about 1 to 4 percent of runs; competing models did not use their own developers' servers.
Researchers believe the behaviour is a training artefact, not a targeted attack, but the routify-file-proxy domain is still live and could log or inject content.
stories.market_take: Limited direct market effect; a reputational issue for Alibaba's AI models that could weigh slightly on sentiment towards Chinese AI.

stories.headline: Fields Medal-winning UC Berkeley professor ends graded homework due to AI cheating
stories.claim: UC Berkeley mathematician Richard Borcherds has stopped grading homework because AI use makes it pointless.
stories.summary: Richard Borcherds, a Fields Medal-winning mathematician at UC Berkeley, has stopped giving graded homework, saying AI use has made it impossible to judge student work. He now relies mainly on in-person, device-free exams, noting that average scores rise in online exams. The article cites research and a Brown University case where take-home midterm averages jumped sharply. UC Berkeley found AI-detection software unreliable and has let professors set their own AI rules in course syllabi.

stories.headline: Apple Shares tvOS 27.2 Release Notes With List of New Features
stories.claim: Apple releases tvOS 27.2 with FaceTime, screen saver and Find My updates, and says Siri AI is not yet enabled on older Apple TV models.
stories.summary: Apple released tvOS 27.2 on Monday for Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) and newer models. The update adds FaceTime links for joining calls from the TV, sign language interpreter and captioning support for third-party services, and a shuffle option for screen saver categories. Find My now works with the Siri Remote (2nd generation) and later, though Precision Finding is limited to the 4th generation remote. Apple said Siri AI will come to older models but it is not yet enabled. The new Apple TV 4K (4th generation) launches on 13 November.

stories.headline: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones
stories.claim: Drone delivery noise is prompting complaints, and firms including Greenjets and Sharrow are developing quieter drone propulsion.
stories.summary: A BBC feature looks at the growing noise complaints from drone deliveries by Amazon Prime Air and Walmart-linked Wing, which are expanding to hundreds of towns and cities in the US and reached Darlington in England. Acoustic experts say the high-pitched whine is especially noticeable, and complaints are likely to grow as the sector expands. The US FAA has been criticised for permitting noisy operations and says local operators and leaders have primary responsibility for community concerns. Start-ups Greenjets, which claims at least a two-thirds noise reduction through enclosed rotors, and Sharrow Engineering, which makes tipless propellers, are developing quieter designs. Amazon says its newer propellers produce almost half the perceived sound of the prior generation.
key_points: Residents near drone delivery routes in the US report irritating buzzing from Amazon and Walmart-linked services.
